Direct-message admission preferences apply only to new exact participant sets; existing one-to-one and group conversations remain available.
Every recipient must allow the creator before a new group direct message can be created.

All notifications includes essential notices plus enabled optional categories; Essential only pauses optional in-app notification creation, hides the individual category controls, and preserves their choices.

Profile Preferences is available from the app sidebar, the desktop profile menu, and the Preferences action in the authenticated user's own profile header.

records.title: Mobile push notifications

records.title: NFT activity feed

records.title: Wave mentions
facts: Wave-name mentions are typed with # plus at least 2 characters and submit as tracked mentioned_waves metadata.
The broadcast mentions @all and @contributors are available only to the Wave creator and profiles in the Admins scope.

The case-insensitive @contributors mention targets profiles with Chat access that joined the Wave and enabled Broadcast mentions, while @admins targets the Wave creator and profiles in the Admins scope.

When Wave Chat access is Public, joined Wave followers with Broadcast mentions enabled are the bounded @contributors audience because there is no finite Chat-access group; muted followers and the author are excluded.
The Broadcast mentions notification preference controls both @all and @contributors, while All messages continues to notify a joined profile about every message.
The @devs6529 mention targets configured 6529 developer profiles that can view the Wave.
Any profile with Chat access can invoke @admins or @devs6529 by typing the complete token directly or selecting it from suggestions; the backend filters recipients by Wave access.

Broadcast suggestions are unavailable to non-admins; if a non-admin types @all or @contributors directly in a new message, the token is posted as ordinary text without broadcast metadata or notifications.

A non-admin can retain @contributors while editing an existing message that already contained it, but the edit does not rebroadcast the mention and they cannot add it as a broadcast mention to a message that did not already contain it.
Global mention text inside links or inline and fenced code remains literal and does not notify a Wave audience.
Editing stored global-mention tokens does not resend permission-group notifications; mentioned_groups describes tokens in the current displayed content, not historical notification delivery.
Global mentions stay visible in posted content; personal Quick Tags expand into individual profile mentions before submission.
Profiles can create private Quick Tags from the owner-only section beneath Activity on their Profile Brain tab; a Quick Tag such as @frens expands inline into ordinary profile mentions.
Quick Tags are case-insensitive, cannot use reserved global mention names, and are not stored in the posted drop after expansion.
Mention behavior depends on composer state, supported metadata, and the user's eligibility in the current wave.
The @help6529 helper bot trigger also uses mention detection, but the bot runtime is implemented in the backend.

Blank or whitespace-only text is not saved as a storm part, while media-only parts are allowed. If a current unsaved part blocks editing saved parts, narrow layouts show an instruction to add or clear it.
An empty Storm draft cannot be posted, Poll and Storm cannot be started together, and the storm is published as one drop with multiple ordered parts.

facts: App wallets management lives at /tools/app-wallets.
In Capacitor, Connect -> App Wallets lists app-local wallets, opens the existing create flow, and connects through the existing unlock flow.
Wallet import lives at /tools/app-wallets/import-wallet and detail pages use /tools/app-wallets/{app-wallet-address}.
Input rules, result states, detail actions, and recovery are documented in the API tool docs.

records.title: Block Finder
facts: Block Finder lives at /tools/block-finder.
It has documented mode and validation rules, loading behavior, result states, and recovery.
Use this tool when users ask how to find a block from supported lookup inputs.

records.title: Delegation write action routes
facts: Delegation write action routes are documented under Delegation docs.
Routes have input, validation, query-parameter, feedback, and transaction-state rules.
Users should start from the Delegation Center when unsure which delegation action to take.

records.title: Delegation collection management
facts: Delegation collection management is documented under Delegation docs.

records.title: Drop Forge craft claims
facts: Drop Forge craft claims live under /drop-forge/craft.
Craft claim detail pages use /drop-forge/craft/{id}.
Craft claims are distinct from launch claims.

records.title: Drop Forge launch claims
facts: Drop Forge launch claims live under /drop-forge/launch.
Launch claim detail pages use /drop-forge/launch/{id}.

If the authorized wallet is disconnected, a launch on-chain action opens wallet connection and continues after connection succeeds when its transaction details are unchanged; refreshed details cancel the pending action so the user can review and retry.
Launch claim pages can include mint stats and subscription airdrop sections when configured.

records.title: Native iOS EULA consent
facts: The native iOS app requires acceptance of the current EULA before application content starts.
EULA acceptance is versioned and valid for 365 days; stale, unversioned, expired, or differently versioned consent requires acceptance again.
A current unexpired device acceptance can restore consent after an iOS reinstall.
If the consent check fails, the iOS app remains blocked and offers Retry. If saving fails, the agreement stays visible so the user can try again.
Users must scroll through the agreement before Agree becomes available, and the mandatory dialog cannot be dismissed without acceptance.
Android and ordinary web sessions are not affected by the native iOS EULA gate.
